name: max_flow_min_cut
author: edba08e8
description: Computes the maximum flow between a source and a sink node with the Edmonds-Karp algorithm, and the minimum cut (the bottleneck edges whose removal would stop all flow). Edge weights are capacities; on unweighted graphs every edge has capacity 1, so the max flow equals the number of edge-disjoint paths. Use for questions like 'where is the bottleneck between A and B?', 'how much can flow from source to sink?' or 'how many independent routes connect A and B?'. Works on directed graphs (edges carry flow forward) and undirected graphs (either direction). Needs node ids (use lookup_node). Returns max_flow, the cut capacity and the top_k cut edges with node ids and labels; returns an error if the sink cannot be reached from the source.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse, e.g. 'airports' or 'lesmis'.

source.description: Node id where the flow starts, e.g. 'MAA'. Use lookup_node to find ids from names.

sink.description: Node id where the flow ends, e.g. 'LHR'. Must differ from source.

top_k.description: How many minimum-cut edges to list (largest capacity first).
